findings.title: Order readiness is not bound to the expected Application configuration
findings.trigger: Either enabled Order Application has its project, destination, repo/path or Helm overrides changed while its previous Synced/Healthy status and successful operation remain. Git targetRevision can remain identical.
findings.observation: The fixed binary returns exit 0 for wrong project, namespace, cluster, source path, repository and changed Helm parameters in each of the two Order leaves: 12 unexpected successes. A wrong project or cluster can also remain a settled healthy configuration. Status resource namespace alone does not bind destination cluster/project.
findings.impact: The new observer can authorize progress using an unrelated or unreconciled configuration despite a matching commit. P0-S3 only-complete-correct-observations requirement is not met. This is an observer gate defect, not evidence of real deployment or unauthorized access.
findings.fix_condition: Bind Order readiness to expected project, destination server/namespace and complete expected source configuration; reject unapproved multi-source/Helm overrides. Require compared/operation source evidence to agree with the intended effective configuration, or explicitly verify an equivalent trusted configuration fingerprint. Add both Order leaf negative tests including same-revision spec drift. Preserve intended legacy three-leaf behavior.

findings.title: Deleting Order Applications are accepted as ready
findings.trigger: An enabled Order Application has metadata.deletionTimestamp and an Argo resources finalizer while its last status is still Synced/Healthy with a successful operation.
findings.observation: Both order-postgresql/deleting-application and order/deleting-application return exit 0. Metadata is entirely ignored by the decoder.
findings.impact: The observer reports successful readiness for a leaf undergoing teardown; it may disappear or cascade-delete its workload immediately afterward. This is not the unavoidable race after observation: the deletion signal is already in the returned JSON.
findings.fix_condition: Reject or keep waiting on nonempty deletionTimestamp before declaring readiness, and cover finalizer-delayed deletion of each new Order leaf with a finite timeout test. Consider the same safe guard for legacy leaves explicitly rather than silently changing compatibility.
